chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Awrama and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥassān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kathīr, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning the saying of
Allah, the Exalted: “And know that whatever you gain of anything, then for Allah is its khums, and for the Messenger, and for the near of kin.”
He said: “Amīr al-Muʾminīn and the Imams عليهم السلام.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.خُمُسَهُ: its one-fifth share designated by Allah
key_terms.لِذِي الْقُرْبَى: for the near relatives, interpreted here as the divinely designated kin
key_terms.لِلرَّسُولِ: belonging to the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: Who are “the near of kin” in the khums verse according to Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This narration interprets the Quranic phrase “and for the near of kin” as referring to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and the Imams عليهم السلام. It presents the verse as evidence for the designated status and entitlement of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام within the divine ordinance of khums.
